issuer.summary: The Foundation terms identify Alto Foundation as a Cayman software provider and Mesh Interface Corp. as the separate Panamanian interface operator. These disclosures improve role transparency, but do not establish an unconditional DUSD repayment obligor, current corporate registration, named principals or holder insolvency priority. Issuer 4.5 is retained provisionally while those accountability and holder-rights gaps remain; code audits and historical peg performance do not establish issuer creditworthiness.

facts: Foundation terms identify Alto Foundation as a Cayman foundation company providing protocol software; no Foundation registration number or named directors/principals established.

The same terms identify Mesh Interface Corp. (Panama) as an independently operated front end under separate agreements; its role is distinct from software provision, protocol administration and token repayment.

The terms describe DUSD as software functionality, disclaim guaranteed payments and do not establish an unconditional Foundation redemption undertaking. Exact contract-access evidence remains separately dated.
Front-end and yield-feature eligibility restrictions are separate from underlying contract access; they are not scored as issuer quality.

The November 2 canonical review found an issuer-reported transparency document, not an independent financial audit or token-reserve solvency opinion. Current financial assurance and issuer-specific insolvency priority remain unestablished.
